notes: Help page (shared with ant111b): the Antigua corn yield trials of Andrews and Herzberg (1985, pp. 339-353), site a factor with 8 levels, block I to IV within each site, plot within block, trt a factor of 12 treatments, harvwt 'the average yield'; ears codes missing values as -9999 and is an alternate response, id is a row id and plot the plot's position in its block (all ignored). No model on the page. Maindonald, Braun and Andrews (2024) Sections 7.1-7.2 (code ch7.qmd at github.com/jhmaindonald/Rcode) and DAAG 3rd ed. Subsection 10.1.3 (scripts/mlm.html) fit ant111b.lmer <- lmer(harvwt ~ 1 + (1 | site), data=ant111b) on ant111b, the block means of treatment 111 (excluded as derived). The proposed model adds the treatments and the blocks within sites, whose labels I to IV repeat across sites, hence site:block.

Help page: 'Each of 20 tasters each assessed three out of the four varieties. The experiment was conducted according to a balanced incomplete block design'; aftertaste is a mark on a scale from 0 (extreme dislike) to 150 (like very much). The help example and Maindonald, Braun and Andrews (2024) Subsection 4.2.2 'A balanced incomplete block design' (code ch4.qmd at github.com/jhmaindonald/Rcode) fit aov(aftertaste ~ product + panelist), the panelists as fixed blocks; they are rendered as a random intercept.

formula: cbind(dead, tot - dead) ~ Cultivar + dose + year + (1 | gp)
notes: Help page: dose-mortality trials of codling moth fumigated with methyl bromide (Maindonald, Waddell and Petry 2001, Postharvest Biology and Technology 22: 99-110); tot is the number of insects in the chamber, dead those dying and pobs their proportion (ignored, derived); gp is 'a factor which has a different level for each different combination of Cultivar, year and rep (replicate)', the replicate series each dose row repeats within; cm and numcm are the series' control mortality and control count, ct the concentration-time sum. No model on the page, in DAAG 3rd ed. or in Maindonald, Braun and Andrews (2024), whose exercise 7.6 fits the companion table sorption by lmer(ct ~ Cultivar + Dose + factor(year) + (-1 + Dose | gp)). The proposed model takes gp as the random intercept and keeps the contract's logit link, although qra (Maindonald) graphs its codling1988 and codling1989 versions of these trials on a complementary log-log scale.

Help page: periods between rain events at Winnipeg International Airport, length 'the length of time from the completion of the last rain event to the beginning of the next rain event' in days, year the calendar year; the examples draw boxplot(length ~ year) and boxplot(log(length) ~ year) and fit no model, and the year grouping is inferred from those boxplots. RULE GAP: one station's record, read as dry spells grouped by year (many events per year, as a sampling month groups squid) rather than as a time series without replication.

Maindonald, Braun and Andrews (2024), Subsection 7.8.1 'Example -- random variation between profiles', paragraph 'A random coefficients model' (code ch7.qmd at github.com/jhmaindonald/Rcode): hp.lmer <- lmer(o2 ~ wattsPerKg + (wattsPerKg | id), data=humanpower1), then hp.lmer <- lmer(o2 ~ wattsPerKg + (0+wattsPerKg | id), data=humanpower1), whose summary the book prints; that final fit is filed, a slope per athlete without a random intercept. DAAG 3rd ed. Subsection 10.6.1 (scripts/mlm.html) prints the correlated fit lmer(o2 ~ wattsPerKg + (wattsPerKg | id)). The help page fits lm(o2 ~ id + wattsPerKg:id); id identifies the five athletes of the Daedalus project trials (Bussolari 1987), o2 is oxygen uptake in ml/min/kg.

Help page: diastolic blood pressure (bp) and sodium excretion (na) of each of 52 populations of the Intersalt study (Intersalt Cooperative Research Group 1988, BMJ 297: 319-328), population medians per the description, each population a sample of 200 individuals; the example plots bp against na, no model. country repeats where a country holds several populations, so the populations are grouped by country, a grouping inferred from the column; b is undocumented ('a numeric vector') and ignored. The response is a population summary, an aggregate on that grouping.

Help page example: kiwishade.lmer <- lmer(yield ~ shade + (1|block) + (1|block:plot), data=kiwishade), commented 'block:shade is an alternative to block:plot', after kiwishade.aov <- aov(yield ~ shade+Error(block/shade)); the same fit in Maindonald, Braun and Andrews (2024) Subsection 7.4.5 'The mixed model analysis' (ch7.qmd at github.com/jhmaindonald/Rcode) and DAAG 3rd ed. Subsection 10.3.5 (scripts/mlm.html). Design: four vines per plot and four plots, one per shading treatment, in each of three blocks (west, north, east), yield the vine's total in kg (Snelgar, Manson and Martin 1992). The plot labels already name their block (east.Aug2Dec), so block:plot groups as plot does.

Help page lists glasshouse (A, B, C), CO2level, day ('a factor'), light, CO2, tempDiff ('Difference between Leaf and Air Temperature'), BtempDiff, airTemp and vapPress, with no model or source paper; in the first rows each day holds one row per glasshouse at one light level. The covariates are those of the parallel-lines fit on leaftemp, lm(tempDiff ~ CO2level + vapPress) (leaftemp's help page; Maindonald, Braun and Andrews 2024, Section 4.3 'Fitting multiple lines', which plots its diagnostics); leaftemp holds these rows without day and is excluded as derived. In the first rows leaftemp's tempDiff matches this table's BtempDiff and the reverse; tempDiff is kept as this page names it, BtempDiff ignored as an alternate response. The day grouping is inferred from the column; glasshouse carries one CO2 level each in the rows shown.

formula: dead ~ dvcat + seatbelt + airbag + frontal + (1 | yearacc:caseid)
notes: Help page: front-seat occupants of US police-reported crashes with a towed vehicle, 1997-2002 (NASS CDS; Meyer and Finney 2005); caseid is 'created by pasting together the populations sampling unit, the case number, and the vehicle number. Within each year, use this to uniquely identify the vehicle', so driver and passenger (occRole) repeat within yearacc:caseid, and the crash (sampling unit and case) has no column of its own. The examples and Maindonald, Braun and Andrews (2024) Chapter 1 tabulate deaths per 1000 by airbag, seatbelt and dvcat (xtabs(weight ~ dvcat + seatbelt + airbag + dead)), with a subset on frontal; no model. weight is the inverse selection probability of the multi-stage sample: the source weights each occupant by it, which the formula leaves out. injSeverity (4 = killed) is an alternate response and deploy codes abcat == 'deploy' (both ignored); dvcat is an ordered factor of estimated impact speed.
